archetype: Naya Dinosaur typal battlecruiser that is RELIANT on its commander, not merely built around him: one engine, Gishath's combat-damage reveal, with three command-zone cost reducers as its ignition, a top-of-library fuel layer, a per-Dinosaur-entry draw layer that pays the reveal back, and a two-card enrage residue (Trapjaw Tyrant, Wrathful Raptors) that survives only as the payoff side of one verified one-sided sweep. Bracket floor 3 on two Game Changers and nothing else.

role_assignment.default_role: Control POSTURE for the first six turns while the mana climbs, and honest about what the posture buys (strategy:whos-the-beatdown). The development is real: 'Ramp or fixing drawn' assembles in 96.4% of goldfish games, 86.4% by turn 6, mean turn 2.335, and mean available mana is 5.96 on turn 6 and 7.527 on turn 8 (goldfish_metrics.json). What the posture cannot claim is a mid-game value line independent of the commander: the enrage web that used to be the second engine is now two converters at 56.7% assembled, 28.1% by turn 6, with no free damage source left in the 99 (goldfish 'Enrage engine drawn'; engine.json). strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection warns that 'experienced tables hit the quiet ramp player', and Forge V3 is the record of that: Gishath's seat was eliminated in 23 of 40 games, nine times by the sythis seat, at a mean global turn 36.17 (sim analysis). The deck owns the long game only once Gishath is on the table and connecting — before that it owns nothing, so per strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock the honest read of inevitability is 'ours after the first resolved connection, theirs before it'.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: A castable Gishath with the connect in hand — evasion or the tapped-out opponent — and a held board-wide protection instant (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window: 'protection up, table tapped out, interaction counted and accounted for'; strategy:pivot-point: 'hold the protection spell for the turn you commit, not after'). The goldfish puts the cast by turn 6 in 25.5% of games, median turn 7, mean 7.362, never by turn 10 in 2,299 of 10,000; Forge V3 resolved him in 32 of 40 games (0.80, CI 0.652–0.895), first at a mean global turn 26.44 (median 25.5, min 18) in a four-seat game — the seventh round at the median. The trigger that says GO is a resolved Gishath plus one of: Rogue's Passage with {4} open, Kessig Wolf Run mana, Enlarge for a fourteen-card reveal, or a Kinjalli's Sunwing already tapping their blockers. Only Flawless Maneuver is free on the turn you tap out for eight; every other shield costs mana the same turn (oracle text). There is no engine-side pivot any more: the Forerunner restart the old frame offered left the deck with the check-in.

engines.engine: THE ENGINE, singular, and VERIFIED in resolution: 'Whenever Gishath deals combat damage to a player, reveal that many cards from the top of your library. Put any number of Dinosaur creature cards from among them onto the battlefield.' Stack 001 (checker pass) resolves one 7-damage connection into four simultaneous entries, three Garruk's Uprising draws and one Pantlaza discover at X=6, with the sequencing lesson that the Regisaur Alpha token trigger is ordered last so it cannot re-trigger Pantlaza's once-per-turn discover. Its stipulated reveal names Ripjaw Raptor, Cultivate and Ravenous Sailback, none of which is in the current 99 — the rules facts survive, the board does not. Density is 30 Dinosaur entries among 34 creature entries (cards.json type lines); the four non-Dinosaurs the reveal bottoms are Huatli, Knight of the Stampede, Otepec Huntmaster and Selvala. Modelled for the first time: the goldfish's commander reveal fired in 7,255 of 10,000 games, 1.953 times a game, for 4.096 free Dinosaurs, at a connect rate of 0.70 per attack that is FORGE'S figure (60 attacks, 42 triggers in the V3 record), not the model's — the model has no blockers. He carries his own haste, vigilance and trample, so the connection kit is about size and evasion, not about attacking at all.
engines.evidence: verified stack 001 (checker pass); goldfish_metrics.json commander_reveal (games_it_fired 7255, mean_fired 1.953, mean_bodies 4.096, connects_per_attack 0.70 sourced to the V3 logs); cards.json type lines (34 creature entries, 30 Dinosaur); sim V3 commander_access (resolved 32/40)

engines.piece: Command-zone ignition (Otepec Huntmaster, Urza's Incubator, Knight of the Stampede)
engines.engine: THE BINDING AXIS, now three cards deep instead of two. All three reduce a SPELL you cast — 'Dinosaur spells you cast cost {1} less' (Otepec), 'Creature spells of the chosen type cost {2} less' (Incubator), 'Dinosaur spells you cast cost {2} less' (Knight) — and a command-zone cast is a cast, so each touches Gishath; together they leave exactly {R}{G}{W}, since the discount is generic only (oracle text). strategy:deckbuilding.curve's clock is the reason this layer decides games: 'unless the majority of your deck is mana ramp... you're probably only going to be able to cast ONE big-mana spell per game', and this deck's one big spell is the whole plan. Each of the three is 'a named card is 7.1% of your opening seven' (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors); no goldfish target measures the three alone — 'Cost reducer or cheat-into-play drawn' reads 81.0% assembled and 64.1% by turn 6 (opening seven 0.412 per deck-audit's component odds) over a SEVEN-card group in which Descendants' Path, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual and Huatli cannot reach the command zone. engine.json's proposed_goldfish_edits asks for the split. Forge V3 (the V3 list, before Knight arrived) cast Otepec 11 times and Incubator 3 in 40 games (sim engine_casts).
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); goldfish_metrics.json targets ('Cost reducer or cheat-into-play drawn' 0.81 / 0.641 / mean turn 3.334); deck-audit engine component odds (size 7, opening_seven 0.412); engine.json proposed_goldfish_edits; sim V3 engine_casts

engines.piece: Fuel: the top of the library (Congregation at Dawn, Worldly Tutor, Enlightened Tutor, Descendants' Path, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual, Huatli's Saga)
engines.engine: The reveal converts only what is on top, so consistency here is bought as strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors describes it — a tutor is 'essentially an additional copy of any card in our deck' — but pointed at ARRANGEMENT rather than at a named card: Congregation at Dawn puts three creatures on top in your order at instant speed, Worldly Tutor one, so the swing after either is a stacked reveal. Descendants' Path casts a Dinosaur free off the top every upkeep you control one; Belbe's Portal ({3}, {T}) and Monster Manual ({1}{G}, {T}) put a creature from HAND onto the battlefield, which skips the cast but not the draw; Huatli's Saga makes two 3/3 Dinosaurs, tutors a third to hand and then grants double strike. None of the doors touches the command zone. The two Game Changers in the deck are both here (Enlightened Tutor, Worldly Tutor — bracket_report.json), which is the whole of the deck's bracket-3 case. Forge V3: Congregation cast 5, Worldly Tutor 6, Enlightened Tutor 5, Descendants' Path 6, Monster Manual cast 7 and activated 7, Belbe's Portal cast 3 and activated 2 (sim engine_casts).
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); bracket_report.json game_changers; sim V3 engine_casts; engine.json fuel stage

engines.piece: Per-entry conversion (Pantlaza, Garruk's Uprising, Vaultborn Tyrant, Earthshaker Dreadmaw, Curious Altisaur, Quartzwood Crasher)
engines.engine: What pays the reveal back in cards, and the layer the check-in strengthened: Earthshaker Dreadmaw draws 'a card for each other Dinosaur you control' on entry, so off a reveal it is a draw-N on a board the reveal just built (unverified in situ — see candidate lines). Pantlaza discovers X = the entering creature's toughness once a turn; Uprising and Vaultborn draw per power-4-or-greater entry, Vaultborn gaining 3 as well; Curious Altisaur draws when any Dinosaur connects; Quartzwood makes an X/X for the trample damage dealt. Stack 001 is the fact tier for Pantlaza and Uprising on simultaneous entries. strategy:card-advantage's Commander correction is the school: 'engines that out-draw three players are the format's defining advantage'. The count the audit sees is 5 copies against the template's '10 card draw' (strategy:deckbuilding.ratios) with Dreadmaw, Jetmir's Garden, Rishkar's Expertise, Runic Armasaur and Vaultborn named as uncounted, and the goldfish models 2 of 8 draw cards, naming Curious Altisaur, Hunter's Insight, Runic Armasaur, Selvala and Vaultborn as unmodelled — so its 1.353 extra cards by turn 8 is a floor on a layer that is mostly dark. 'Dinosaur payoff drawn' reads 84.9% assembled, 60.4% by turn 6, mean turn 3.985, over a six-card group that omits Vaultborn and Dreadmaw.
engines.evidence: verified stack 001 (checker pass); oracle text; deck-audit card-advantage axis (5 vs 10, possible_uncounted); goldfish_metrics.json meta.card_advantage (modelled 2 of 8) and targets; engine.json proposed_goldfish_edits

engines.piece: Blasphemous Act + Temple Altisaur, with the enrage residue (Wrathful Raptors, Trapjaw Tyrant)
engines.engine: VERIFIED, and the one asymmetric sweep the deck owns — exactly the effect strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry says to prefer: 'asymmetric board wipes ... and effects that tax or drain every opponent at once'. Temple Altisaur is a shield, not a payoff: 'If a source would deal damage to another Dinosaur you control, prevent all but 1 of that damage.' Stack 004 (checker pass) resolves the Act cast for {R} off nine creatures: Altisaur is not 'another Dinosaur' to itself, takes 13 and dies; every other Dinosaur is dealt exactly 1 and lives; state-based actions clear the opponents' creatures BEFORE Wrathful's redirects choose targets, so 16 damage (13 by last known information plus 1 each from three survivors) can only go at players — 26 to 10, not lethal. Trapjaw Tyrant's exile off the 1 that gets through is the same trigger shape and is NOT on stack 004's board, and stack 004's board carries Ripjaw Raptor, which left. What the line costs is drawing both halves: 8.1% assembled, 1.8% by turn 6, mean turn 7.708, 29.9% tutor-assisted, each half a single card at 7.1% of an opening seven, and deck-audit names Blasphemous Act the deck's single point of failure. This is the reason to keep four cards, not a plan. The two converters without the Act are a 13.7%-of-openers pair (deck-audit component odds) that converts nothing: the only card in the 99 that marks damage on your own Dinosaurs without spending a removal spell on yourself is the Act (engine.json).
engines.evidence: verified stack 004 (checker pass); goldfish_metrics.json ('THE ONE-SIDED APOCALYPSE' 0.081 / 0.018 / mean turn 7.708 / assisted 0.299); deck-audit single_points_of_failure (Blasphemous Act, opening_seven 0.071) and 'Enrage engine drawn' component (size 2, opening_seven 0.137); oracle text

engines.piece: The mana climb (35 land copies + 4 rocks + 3 land-ramp sorceries + Mirari's Wake, Regal Behemoth, Selvala, Hulking Raptor, Topiary Stomper, Wayward Swordtooth)
engines.engine: Budgeted the way strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base says to — 'Budget mana sources, not lands' — the deck clears the Burgess line 'lands = 31 + colours in the commander's identity + the commander's mana value' (31 + 3 + 8 = 42) with 45 counted sources (deck-audit mana-sources), while the 35 land copies sit one under the template's '36–38 lands' (strategy:deckbuilding.ratios). deck-audit's ramp axis reads 15 against '10–12 ramp' and calls it over, but read the list before agreeing: it counts Blasphemous Act (its discount is its own cost) and Bonehoard Dracosaur (Treasure) and does not count Skyshroud Claim, Selvala, Regal Behemoth or Wayward Swordtooth — the axis is a role count, not a source count. The strain is colour, not quantity: land sources G22/R18/W17 lift to G26/R21/W21 with rocks and dorks, against the audit's 36-per-colour Karsten target (worst colour −15), and mana_analysis puts the on-curve rate with rocks and dorks at W 0.61, R 0.61, G 0.742. Gishath's own pips are single in each colour and late, the shape strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base.color-sources calls cheapest ('the requirement falls fast as the spell gets later'); what the 21 white sources cannot promise on curve is Wakening Sun's Avatar's WWW ('37 for {C}{C}{C}', and 'triple pips and three colours do not coexist'), Austere Command's and Trapjaw's WW. 12 of 35 lands enter tapped, 7 unconditionally, against 'around eight taplands is comfortable in a slow deck'. Consistency holds: 89.4% hit the turn-3 land drop, 78.0% of first sevens are keepable, but the land-drop rate falls to 55.5% by turn 6 and the deck then rides the nonland layer — 5.96 mean mana on turn 6 — which is the layer a sweeper takes. Unclaimed Territory pays Gishath and cannot pay Rogue's Passage or Kessig Wolf Run; Secluded Courtyard's clause does pay abilities (deck-facts notes).
engines.evidence: deck-audit axes (mana-base 35, mana-sources 45 vs 42, ramp 15 with its card list, taplands 7, colour-sources −15, consistency 0.894); mana_analysis.json (sources, on_curve_probability, enters_tapped 12 / always 7); goldfish_metrics.json (land_drop_hit_rate t3 0.894 / t6 0.555, mean_available_mana t6 5.96 / t8 7.527, keep_first_seven_rate 0.78); deck-facts mana and notes

engines.piece: The connection kit (Rogue's Passage, Kessig Wolf Run, Enlarge, Kinjalli's Sunwing, Sunfrill Imitator, Boros Charm's double strike, Huatli's chapter IV)
engines.engine: Gishath has haste, vigilance and trample printed on him, so the kit's job is to make the hit land and make it bigger: Rogue's Passage ({4}: can't be blocked) and Kessig Wolf Run (+X/+0) are lands and survive a wrath; Enlarge is +7/+7 and 'must be blocked this turn if able' — a fourteen-card reveal if the blocker is small enough to trample over, and a forced chump if it is not; Kinjalli's Sunwing makes 'creatures your opponents control enter tapped', which strips the flashed-in blocker; Sunfrill Imitator attacking beside him may become a copy of Gishath (unverified — candidate line); Boros Charm's double strike and Huatli's chapter IV are a second damage step and, plausibly, a second reveal (unverified). Forge V3 is the only measurement of the connection itself: 0.70 triggers per attack, 42 in 40 games, Rogue's Passage activated 10 times and Kessig 3, and Gishath's damage reached 21 on one defender in 4 of 40 games (commander_damage games_reaching_21 0.10) — strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry lists 'commander-damage kills' among 'the payoffs that actually scale', and here it is a side effect, not the plan. The goldfish's 'connection kit' target (79.2% assembled, 60.3% by turn 6) is scoped to haste-or-evasion and omits Enlarge, Sunwing and Imitator; engine.json proposes the rescope.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json); sim V3 (commander_reveal source note: 60 attacks / 42 triggers; commander_damage games_reaching_21 4 of 40; engine_casts Rogue's Passage 10, Kessig 3); goldfish_metrics.json targets; engine.json open_questions and proposed_goldfish_edits

engines.piece: Protection (Akroma's Will, Heroic Intervention, Flawless Maneuver, Boros Charm, Eerie Interlude; Carnage Tyrant by role)
engines.engine: Insurance on the hub, priced as strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance prices it: 'each return trip to the command zone adds {2} per prior command-zone cast' on top of eight, and Forge V3 shows the tax being paid — 49 Gishath casts in 40 games, a mean of 1.23 per game (sim commander_access), so the second cast was the norm. Six copies by role sit inside the doc's '5-7 protection slots' (strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density); the five instants assemble at 70.0%, 51.1% by turn 6. Read them rather than count them: Heroic Intervention's hexproof and Akroma's Will's protection from each colour cover targeted exile and bounce; Eerie Interlude is the only one that dodges a non-targeted mass exile and, cast into a wrath, returns the board at end step as one simultaneous entry into the conversion layer (unverified — candidate line); Flawless Maneuver is the only one castable for nothing on the turn you tap out for eight. Cullen's decision test in the same section — 'how critical is the commander to the plan' — has an unusual answer here: entirely, so the section's 'racing alternative' of skipping insurance does not apply.
engines.evidence: deck-audit protection axis (6 copies, target 5-7); goldfish_metrics.json ('Protection held for the board' 0.70 / 0.511 / mean turn 3.846); sim V3 commander_access (casts mean 1.23, 49 casts / 40 games); oracle text

engines.piece: Interaction (9 removal copies inside a 16-card suite; 2 sweepers; breadth 4 of 5)
engines.engine: At Walser's floor — 'at least 8-10 removal spells' inside a '15- to 20-card interactive suite' (strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite) — with 9 and 16, and 2 sweepers inside 'one or two max'. Breadth lost a class with the check-in: Intrepid Paleontologist was the deck's only graveyard answer, so the audit now reads graveyard uncovered against 'cover the classes — creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land — before doubling any', and land coverage still rests on Beast Within alone. Two of the removal pieces are enrage-dependent (Trapjaw) or discard-mode (Trumpeting Carnosaur, which Forge V3 discarded 6 times and cast once). The table-facing fact is Forge's: Gishath's seat cast a mean of 0.5 interaction spells a game and received 0.65 (sim analysis) — the deck's answers mostly stayed in hand while its commander did the work, which is strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy's 'hold single-target removal until the threat is pointed at you' applied by an AI that could not tell when it was.
engines.evidence: deck-audit axes (interaction 9, interactive_suite_copies 16, sweepers 2, interaction-breadth 4 with uncovered ['graveyard']); sim V3 analysis (interaction_cast mean 0.5, interaction_received 0.65; engine_casts Trumpeting Carnosaur cast 1 / discarded 6); oracle text

engines.piece: The trample swing (Overwhelming Stampede, Ghalta, Primal Hunger, Ghalta and Mavren, Regal Imperiosaur, Regisaur Alpha, Carnage Tyrant, Pugnacious Hammerskull)
engines.engine: How the board the reveal built ends the game. Overwhelming Stampede is +X/+X and trample where X is your greatest power — at least 7 with Gishath out; Ghalta costs {G}{G} off any board the reveal built; Ghalta and Mavren makes an X/X tapped-and-attacking trampler every swing; Regisaur Alpha gives haste to Dinosaurs that entered precombat (stack 001 shows the reveal's own bodies cannot attack the combat they arrive in). Measured with model_combat on, one opponent, no blockers: kill by turn 6 5.8%, turn 7 29.3%, turn 8 61.7%, turn 10 90.5%, mean kill turn 8.03, median 8 (goldfish combat) — the goldfish's no-blockers caveat makes this a ceiling on tempo, not a forecast. Forge V3 against the standard table: 12 wins of 35 decided, 0.343 with CI 0.208–0.508, an interval that contains the '~25% of games by default' strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density gives a four-player seat; combat damage to players mean 71.03 but median 28 (a mean is not a result); and the winner-seat count was 11 firsts against 8 fourths. No checker-passed stack resolves a lethal swing (engine.json open question).
engines.evidence: goldfish_metrics.json combat (kill_by_turn_rate, mean_kill_turn 8.03, median 8, mean_board_power t8 31.555); sim V3 analysis (win_rate 0.343 CI [0.208, 0.508], decided 35, combat_damage_dealt_to_players mean 71.03 / median 28, placement 11 firsts / 8 fourths); verified stack 001 on haste timing; oracle text

candidate_missing_lines.title: Sunfrill Imitator attacks beside Gishath and becomes a copy of him: does the copy reveal on its own connection this combat?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Sunfrill Imitator reads 'Whenever this creature attacks, you may have it become a copy of another target Dinosaur you control, except its name is Sunfrill Imitator and it has this ability.' A copy of Gishath would carry the combat-damage reveal, a 7/6 body and vigilance/trample/haste, and the differing name should keep the legend rule off. If it holds, the deck's single point of failure has a {2}{G} second copy on the attack, and engine.json already files the question. Copy timing on an attacking creature, whether the copy's 7 power is what deals damage, and the legend-rule reading all need the checker before any number goes in print.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Blasphemous Act through Temple Altisaur with BOTH surviving converters on a board this 99 can produce
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Stack 004's board carries Ripjaw Raptor, which left the deck, and has no Trapjaw Tyrant; stack 005's board (Forerunner, Ranging Raptors, Ripjaw, Polyraptor) is no longer this deck's at all. Stack 004 establishes that a prevented-down-to-1 hit is still 'dealt damage' and fires Wrathful, and Trapjaw's enrage has the same trigger condition, so one Act plausibly exiles one creature per opponent-facing Trapjaw trigger AND redirects; the ordering of Trapjaw's exile against the state-based-action sweep that clears the targets is the open rules question. The per-card verified index still credits Trapjaw to a board the deck cannot reach.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Earthshaker Dreadmaw arriving off the reveal: does 'each other Dinosaur you control' count the Dinosaurs entering with it?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Dreadmaw reads 'When this creature enters, draw a card for each other Dinosaur you control', and stack 001 establishes that the reveal puts every chosen Dinosaur onto the battlefield as ONE event. If the count is taken on resolution it includes the simultaneous arrivals plus Gishath and the standing board, which would make Dreadmaw the largest single draw the reveal can free-roll; it also stacks against Pantlaza's once-per-turn discover (X = 6 for Dreadmaw's toughness) and Uprising's per-entry draws. Nothing in the artifact set resolves it and the goldfish names the per-entry draw layer as mostly unmodelled.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Boros Charm's double strike on a connecting Gishath: two combat-damage steps, two reveals?
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Boros Charm's third mode is 'Target creature gains double strike until end of turn', and Gishath's trigger is 'Whenever Gishath deals combat damage to a player'. Double strike deals combat damage in the first-strike step and again in the regular step, which should be two separate damage events and two triggers of seven each, with the first reveal's bodies on the battlefield before the second connection. Huatli's chapter IV grants the same to every Dinosaur. engine.json calls Boros Charm 'a second reveal' as a claim; no stack has resolved it.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Eerie Interlude in response to a wrath, with the per-entry layer down
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Interlude returns the exiled creatures 'at the beginning of the next end step' as one event, which re-fires every entry trigger in the conversion layer at once — engine.json draws the arrow dashed and files the question. A pass would make the deck's cheapest insurance also its best re-trigger; the count of Uprising and Vaultborn draws, the Dreadmaw draw, and the single Pantlaza discover and its X all need the checker.

candidate_missing_lines.title: What board actually kills a 40-life opponent, and from how far
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: No checker-passed stack resolves a lethal swing; the closest measurement is stack 004's 16 redirected damage taking one opponent from 26 to 10. The goldfish's kill-by-turn-8 of 0.617 is against one opponent with no blockers, and Forge V3's commander damage reached 21 on one defender in 4 of 40 games. A worked lethal — Stampede's +X/+X over a revealed board, or Enlarge on Gishath into a forced block — is the arrow every wincon line in engine.json leaves dashed.

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: The worst frame, and the check-in made it worse by removing the cheap rebuild. 'Deploy in waves' (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math) is structurally unavailable when the commander's trigger IS the wave, and a wipe takes the nonland mana with the board — Huatli and Hulking Raptor (the two dorks by role), Selvala, Regal Behemoth and Mirari's Wake — which is why the deck rides 5.96 mean mana on turn 6 after the land-drop rate falls to 55.5%. Duke's rule in the same section is the discipline: 'commit exactly as much as wins before it arrives, no further', so hold Dinosaurs in hand behind a resolved Gishath rather than in front of him, swing only with a board-wide instant held (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window), and 'let another player's board be the reason it gets cast'. After the wrath 'initiative goes to whoever rebuilds cheapest', and the honest rebuild here is the commander again at 8 plus '{2} per prior command-zone cast' (strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance) — Forge V3 paid that tax in most games (49 casts, 40 games). Forge's sythis seat, the pod's enchantment-control deck, eliminated Gishath in 9 of the 23 games he was eliminated in (sim analysis eliminated_by). Temple Altisaur's damage floor is verified against the deck's own Act (stack 004) and unverified against anyone else's sweeper.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Taxes hit an eight-drop hardest, and the three reducers are the deck's tax-resilience: under a Sphere effect the Otepec + Incubator + Knight trio still leaves Gishath at {R}{G}{W} plus the tax (oracle text), which is the difference between castable and not. strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial forces the role — 'you rarely own the long game under an assembling lock, so you are the beatdown, racing the lock's completion' — and says to 'name your outs early': Beast Within, Thrashing Brontodon and Zacama's {2}{G} mode are the artifact/enchantment answers, Austere Command the reset. Mulligan toward the enabler class, not a named card (strategy:mulligans.engine-hands: 'you mulligan to enabler classes'); the class here is 'a ramp piece plus a reducer', and 'Ramp or fixing drawn' at 63.9% of opening sevens (deck-audit component odds) is what the keep rests on. Unclaimed Territory cannot pay an activated ability under any tax (deck-facts notes). Against a lock on creature entry (a Torpor Orb effect), the reveal still puts bodies down but the conversion layer goes dark — plan on the trample swing, not on the draws.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: The deck owns the long game once Gishath resolves (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock: 'four-player games trend long, so inevitability compounds') and should take the control role until then — but from a body count of 2.825 at turn 6 (goldfish mean_bodies), it holds the ground with toughness, not numbers: Runic Armasaur 2/5, Curious Altisaur 2/5, Temple Altisaur 3/4, Kinjalli's Sunwing 2/3 flying, and Sunwing's tapped-entry text blanks haste creatures outright. Blasphemous Act through Temple Altisaur is the verified answer to a go-wide board (stack 004) and assembles in 8.1% of games — 'be delighted by' it, do not plan on it. Turn the corner the turn Gishath connects (strategy:combat-math.racing: 'the moment you stabilize, flip to offense'), and remember the section's Commander correction — 'you cannot race three life totals' — so the connection goes at the seat that is racing YOU, and Sunwing keeps the other two off tempo.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: The bad seat: no counterspells in Naya, 9 removal copies and 2 sweepers, and a clock that starts when an eight-drop resolves at a median goldfish turn 7 and a Forge median global turn 25.5. strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy: against combo 'the last profitable moment is now', so spend Path, Swords and Beast Within on enablers as they land rather than banking them for a payoff that may never be targetable; strategy:whos-the-beatdown says take the beatdown role regardless of posture — 'whoever loses the long game must be the beatdown'. The honest race is Gishath plus the connection kit, and the honest mulligan is toward the reducers and ramp rather than toward payoffs. Forge V3's abaddon seat (grixis value / sacrifice) eliminated Gishath 6 times; the record has no dedicated combo seat, so this frame is doctrine, not measurement.

distribution_notes: 65 nonland entries over 35 land copies (24 land entries, 89 entries, 100 copies — deck-facts counts). Curve by nonland entry: 6 at one, 8 at two, 19 at three, 7 at four, 11 at five, 7 at six, 2 at seven, 2 at eight, 2 at nine and one at twelve (deck-facts curve) — modal mana value 3 against the '~1.5 cards at mana value 8+' of an average deck (strategy:deckbuilding.curve), this deck holding five, one of them the plan. 34 creature entries, 30 Dinosaurs (cards.json). Goldfish (10,000 iterations, seed 42, decklist sha b394917f7b1b, model_combat and model_treasures on, commander reveal declared): ramp/fixing 96.4% assembled / 86.4% by turn 6 / mean turn 2.335; cost reducer or cheat 81.0% / 64.1% / 3.334 (seven cards, four of which cannot touch the command zone); Dinosaur payoff 84.9% / 60.4% / 3.985; connection kit 79.2% / 60.3% / 3.543; enrage residue 56.7% / 28.1% / 5.705 (two cards, no damage source declared); protection 70.0% / 51.1% / 3.846; Act + Altisaur 8.1% / 1.8% / 7.708. key_tensions: RELIANT, NOT BUILT AROUND. strategy:deckbuilding.archetype-selection draws Walser's line — 'built around your commander is not reliant on it' — and this list is on the reliant side: engine.json's ignition stage has one single point of failure and it is the commander, the enrage web that was the combat-independent second engine left with Forerunner, Polyraptor, Ripjaw and Ranging Raptors, and every conversion piece waits on a body entering or connecting — Pantlaza, Curious Altisaur and Dreadmaw on a Dinosaur, Uprising and Vaultborn on power 4 or greater, Quartzwood on trample damage (oracle text). The section's remedy is 'redundant copies ... or protection'; the deck bought protection (six copies, 70.0% held) and, with Sunfrill Imitator, possibly one unverified copy. Forge V3 measured the dependence directly: Gishath was cast 49 times in 40 games, and the seat's first attack came at a mean global turn 20.29 — the sixth round of a four-seat game — before him.

IGNITION IS THREE NAMED CARDS AND NOTHING MEASURES THE THREE. Otepec Huntmaster, Urza's Incubator and Knight of the Stampede are the only cards that make a command-zone cast cheaper; each is 'a named card is 7.1% of your opening seven' (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors). The goldfish target that contains them is a seven-card group at 81.0% assembled whose other four members move Dinosaurs from hand or library and cannot touch Gishath. The goldfish also now models cost reduction, and the cast still lands at median turn 7 with 23.0% of games never casting him by turn 10, while strategy:deckbuilding.curve says 'Commander games average 7–10 turns' — the plan resolves inside the average game's last third. engine.json's proposed_goldfish_edits asks for a three-card 'Command-zone discount drawn' target; until it exists, the ignition rate is not a measured number.

THE ENRAGE RESIDUE CONVERTS NOTHING ON ITS OWN. Trapjaw Tyrant and Wrathful Raptors are a two-card class (13.7% of openers, deck-audit component odds) that needs damage marked on your own Dinosaurs, and the only card in the 99 that does that without spending a removal spell on your own creature is Blasphemous Act (engine.json conversion stage; Itzquinth, Triumphant Chomp, Zacama's {2}{R} and Trumpeting Carnosaur's discard all target). The goldfish's 'Enrage engine drawn' still measures the pair alone at 56.7% and describes an engine the list no longer runs; strategy:mulligans.engine-hands: 'Payoffs without the enabler are blanks until the engine exists.' Keep both for the stack-004 line and for Wrathful's 5/5 trample body; do not keep a hand for them.

THE DRAW LAYER IS REAL AND MOSTLY DARK. deck-audit reads card advantage at 5 copies against '10 card draw' (strategy:deckbuilding.ratios) and names five uncounted cards; the goldfish models 2 of 8 draw cards and lists Curious Altisaur, Hunter's Insight, Runic Armasaur, Selvala and Vaultborn as unmodelled; Earthshaker Dreadmaw's draw-N and Pantlaza's discover are keyed to the reveal's 4.096 free bodies a game, which the model only started counting today. So 'extra cards drawn by turn 8: 1.353' is a floor on the stage that pays the reveal back, not a finding that the deck does not draw. strategy:card-advantage's 'engines that out-draw three players' is the school this layer belongs to, and no artifact yet prices it.

SWEEPER EXPOSURE RUNS THROUGH THE MANA, NOT THE LANDS. 35 land copies is an ordinary count and the three land-ramp sorceries bank on the wrath-proof side. What a wipe takes is the nonland layer the deck rides after the land-drop rate falls to 55.5% by turn 6: 4 rocks to an artifact sweep, Hulking Raptor, Selvala, Regal Behemoth and Huatli to any creature wipe. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math: 'commit exactly as much as wins before it arrives, no further' — and with no cheap rebuild engine left, 'whoever rebuilds cheapest' is not this deck unless Gishath is the rebuild.

THE BRACKET STORY IS SIMPLE NOW. bracket_report.json computes floor 3 on a single driver — two Game Changers, Enlightened Tutor and Worldly Tutor — with zero two-card infinites and zero contained combo lines (deck-facts combos). The Polyraptor + Forerunner pairing that drove the old floor of 4 left with the check-in, so the pregame conversation strategy:deckbuilding.power-level describes ('a tool to guide pregame conversations') is a plain one: bracket 3, two of the three Game Changers it allows, an eight-mana commander, and a Forge win rate whose interval contains the default quarter share.

GRAVEYARD IS UNCOVERED. Intrepid Paleontologist was the only graveyard answer and left; the audit's breadth axis now reads 4 of 5 with graveyard named, against strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite's 'cover the classes ... before doubling any'. Forge V3's jarad seat is graveyard midrange and won 4 of 35 decided games; the deck's plan against it is the clock, not an answer.
overall_assessment: This is a commander-reliant battlecruiser playing the critical-mass game with one threshold (strategy:critical-mass): reach a cheaper eight — three named reducers, 'the ONE big-mana spell per game' of strategy:deckbuilding.curve — connect once, and let the reveal build the board that the per-entry layer pays for and the trample layer closes with. The check-in traded the enrage web's combat-independent second engine for cards that serve the first: a third command-zone reducer (Knight of the Stampede), a blocker-stripper (Kinjalli's Sunwing), a reveal multiplier (Enlarge), a draw-N that free-rolls off the reveal (Earthshaker Dreadmaw), a possible second Gishath on the attack (Sunfrill Imitator, unverified) and a draw body that blocks (Runic Armasaur). The deck is now honest about what it is — 'built around your commander is not reliant on it' (strategy:deckbuilding.archetype-selection) and this one is reliant — and the artifacts agree: the goldfish's newly modelled reveal fires 1.953 times a game for 4.096 free Dinosaurs and puts kill-by-turn-8 at 0.617 with no blockers, Forge V3 resolved Gishath in 80% of games and won 0.343 at standard-v3 (CI 0.208–0.508) on the previous list, and the one verified non-commander line, Blasphemous Act through Temple Altisaur into Wrathful Raptors (stack 004), assembles in 8.1% of games. Posture follows from that: quiet development that the table will discount (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection), a pivot that is one card and one protection spell (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window), and insurance paid at '{2} per prior command-zone cast' when it fails (strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance). Its interaction is at Walser's floor with one class uncovered, its draw layer is real and mostly unmodelled, its mana clears the Burgess source line and misses the colour line, and its bracket is a plain 3. Two structural weaknesses stand: the pivot is late — median turn 7 in the goldfish, round seven in Forge — and everything before it is posture.
gaps: No section on commander-RELIANT construction as a school: what changes in mulligans, protection sizing, and pivot timing when the commander is the only engine rather than one of two. strategy:deckbuilding.archetype-selection draws the line in one sentence and stops; this deck needed a whole treatment.

Only a reducer touches a command-zone cast; a goldfish group of seven can read 81% while the three cards that answer the hard half are unmeasured. The doc has no arithmetic for a three-card class either — strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors prices 1, 5, 7, 10 and 20 copies.
